pairs.why: A's coil and loop lie flat on one surface, joined by a knot, while B's open loop stands upright on its own with a cast shadow and connects only through a floating ferrule.
A's clamp grips a truss that runs across the frame, and the yoke pivots plausibly on the can, while B's short truss segment floats in empty air with nothing holding it up.
B's labelled keys sit in rows that follow the tilted face, while A's grid of blank keys could not work as a calculator.
B's tabletop, pedestal and stools share one camera, while A's board-top looks rotated against its front-facing pedestal and base.
B's armrests rest on frame posts running down into the X-legs, while A's orange armrests hang off a frameless fabric back with weak front support.
